Demoed request-level tracing, how to correlate request IDs with KV cache hits, and configuring alerts for elevated error rate. Customer concerned about SOC2 controls, VPC private deployment, and performance on bursty traffic. Agreed next steps to run a short benchmark and provide sandbox access.
transcript:
HEADER: 2026-09-18 14:00 PDT | Duration 46m | Attendees: Jordan Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Desai (Redwood SE), Liam O'Connor (Nebula CTO), Sara Patel (Head of ML), Tom Ruiz (DevOps)

[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone thanks for joining, um we're gonna run through the console tracing and request logs and show a couple debugging flows, feel free to interrupt — is this still a good time?
[00:06] Liam: yeah good, 14:00 works. quick context, we're seeing occasional spikes in latency and some 500-ish errors in production, want to see how we'd triage.
[00:14] Priya: perfect, thanks. i'll share my screen — okay can you all see the Redwood console? looks like the Nebula sandbox org is provisioned.
[00:24] Sara: yep visible. one quick Q: our stack is k8s on-prem, and we use a mixture of hosted and dedicated endpoints, that right?
[00:32] Jordan: right, and on the pricing side you mentioned interested in dedicated for predictable throughput — we'll follow up on that. for this demo we'll focus on tracing + request logs for hosted first then show parity for dedicated.
[00:45] Priya: jumping into tracing — top left is the trace explorer, you can filter by request id, model, route, and time window. i want to show an example trace where latency spiked. clicking into request id req_0a1b...
[00:58] Priya: you can see timeline of stages: gateway -> shard router -> runtime -> kv-cache lookup -> token generation. notice here a long CPU queuing step, about 320ms.
[01:12] Tom: is that queuing at our end or on Redwood?
[01:15] Priya: good Q — the trace includes host tags, region, and whether it was served from dedicated pool. this one was hosted us-west2. there's a note 'batch size 32' which increased scheduling time.
[01:26] Jordan: sometimes batch size spikes due to sudden concurrency; Redwood's autoscaler can burst but queuing shows in the trace. you can set per-route max_batch to control tail latency.
[01:38] Sara: can we see KV cache hits? some errors happen when cache misses cause full context regen.
[01:44] Priya: yeah, expand the cache section — here KV hit=false, miss reason=prefix-mismatch. we also log the prefix hash and the prefix length, so you can correlate with the prompt sent.
[01:58] Liam: nice. how does this tie to request logs?
[02:02] Priya: request logs are queryable log-lines with request_id, model, duration, token_count, error_code, and upload of raw prompt (if retention allows). i can open request logs view and filter by request id to show the raw payload.
[02:18] Priya: (opens logs) here's the request line, you can see we truncated user PII per your data-retention policy — note we support masked prompts in logs.
[02:30] Tom: about retention — Nebula needs 90-day logs for audits, is that configurable?
[02:34] Jordan: yep retention is configurable per org and per export; for Private we can integrate with your S3/GCS with lifecycle rules. SOC2 note: audits include immutable append-only logs and we can provide certified export.
[02:50] Sara: good — also are logs encrypted at rest?
[02:53] Priya: yes, we support KMS/HSM. in the console security tab you can see KMS key id used for this workspace.
[03:02] Liam: ok back to debugging flows, what about errors that look transient — 502s or runtime OOMs?
[03:08] Priya: we demo a 502 example. in trace you see runtime returned 502 with message "token overflow" — expanding the error analysis shows stack trace snippet and the model variant used (gptj-16k-quant).
[03:24] Priya: we also show the fallback policy: if error rate > threshold then route to smaller model or retry with lower max_tokens. that is configured in rollout policies.
[03:35] Sara: are retries automatic or do we recommend app-level retries?
[03:38] Jordan: we provide both — platform-level automatic retries for safe idempotent calls, and you can set client-side retry logic. for stateful calls (e.g., streaming) we recommend app-level approach.
[03:50] Priya: next i'm going to simulate a tail-latency spike using our synthetic load in the sandbox so you can see live traces. starting the job...
[04:00] [04:00] synthetic job kicked off — we see a burst of 200 concurrent requests
[04:12] Priya: traces start streaming in, filter by route /nebula/analysis — here's one with 1.2s tail. check the histogram tab, tail is 95th 1.1s, 99th 1.6s.
[04:26] Tom: what's the quick mitigation?
[04:28] Priya: immediate mitigation: reduce max_batch for that route, enable prefix caching for common prompts, or route burst to dedicated pool. longer term: tune kernel selection and model quantization for lower p99.
[04:42] Liam: can we alert on rising p95?
[04:44] Priya: yes alerts: create metric alert for p95 latency over 500ms for 5m, action webhook to PagerDuty. i'll show where to create that.
[04:55] [06:00] (minutes elided — walkthrough of creating alert, setting webhook)
[10:12] Priya: now request logs correlate with traces — you can click "open in logs" from any trace span and see full set of logs for that request including runtime stderr.
[10:25] Sara: sometimes our DevOps can't find the request id in logs because it's sampled, can we increase sampling?
[10:31] Priya: sampling rate is adjustable per workspace; default is 10% for high-volume routes. we can bump to 100% for a debugging window.
[10:42] Tom: what about costs — storing 100% logs sounds expensive.
[10:45] Jordan: yep tradeoff — we recommend exporting high-fidelity logs to your S3 and keep index in console to reduce per-token retention cost. Optimize ties into this by suggesting what to keep.
[11:00] Liam: for compliance we need an audit trail of changes to rollout policies and KMS key rotations. is that in console?
[11:07] Priya: yes the audit log shows config changes with user and timestamp, and we persist for configured retention. can export to SIEM.
[11:16] Sara: demo request: can you show a real-world example where KV cache caused a silent regression?
[11:20] Priya: sure — open this trace from last week, it shows KV hit=true for older model variant, but after a rollout the key format changed and hit=false leading to increased token usage. console flagged a quality regression because evals on our prompt set showed token delta.
[11:38] Jordan: that was part of the reason we added the prefix-hash diff view — you can diff two model versions and see the expected KV footprint.
[11:48] Tom: any automated remediation?
[11:50] Priya: we have a fallback that routes to previous model variant if cache hit rate drops below threshold for 5 minutes. you can customize window.
[12:02] Sara: excellent. a few practical asks — can Priya provide the quick commands to pull logs via API?
[12:07] Priya: yes, there's an API endpoint /v1/logs?request_id=... i'll copy the curl in chat. also sending a shared sheet with recommended thresholds.
[12:16] Jordan: i'll put the pricing and dedicated node configs after the call.
[12:20] Liam: timeframe — we want a pilot next month, three-week POC, will need dedicated nodes and SOC2 docs to proceed.
[12:28] Jordan: makes sense, we'll send SOC2 package and a POC plan.
[12:34] [13:00] (final wrap up; recap next steps)
[13:12] Jordan: recap — Priya shares sandbox + logs, Jordan sends pricing & SOC2, Nebula runs 10k request benchmark and shares results. agreed next call Tues 2026-09-23 10:00am PT.
[13:28] Sara: thanks all.
[13:31] Liam: thanks, bye.

NOTES: Shared artifacts referenced — sandbox link (https://redwood.example/sandbox/nebula), SOC2 package (link sent post-call), benchmark sheet (drive: /nebula/benchmarks).

END OF TRANSCRIPT
